issue.title: rfserver trusts X-Forwarded-For for its auth-suspension bucket, so token guesses are never suspended

task_type_fields.impact:
Brute-force protection for the static `/sendmail` token works only per spoofable header
value. After the loopback bind, only local accounts can reach it. Athena was compromised
through a service account on 2026-10-17, and a local foothold could guess the token without
limit and use Athena as a mail relay.
task_type_fields.repro:
`/home/bryan/db/bin/main/rfuncs/path_dispatcher.py` `_get_client_address` (line ~64) returns
`environ["HTTP_X_FORWARDED_FOR"].split(",")[-1]` whenever that header is present, and falls
back to `REMOTE_ADDR` otherwise. `Authenticator.check` keys its suspension bucket (more than 10
failed attempts in 10 minutes means SUSPENDED) on that address.

Any client can send a fresh `X-Forwarded-For` value on each request. Its token guesses then
never reach the suspension limit, and it can also exhaust another address's bucket. No proxy
fronts rfserver: since bob-cli-aw (epic bob-cli-an.6, phase 6.4) it binds `127.0.0.1:23401`
only, and the router does not forward 23401.

Fix: ignore `X-Forwarded-For` and use `REMOTE_ADDR` only. Add a regression next to
`~/db/bin/tests/test_rfserver.py`. Source constraint: `~/db/bin` is a long-dirty local
checkout of `bbugyi200/scripts` that SASE cannot open, so the bob-cli-aw edit was applied in
place. Its durable copy is tailnet `hosts/athena/rfserver/` (`server-loopback.patch`,
`tests/test_rfserver_boundary.py`, README). Add this change to that record the same way,
then restart only `tools:rfserver`. Proposed by phase bob-cli-an.6.4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP).

issue.creation_reason: Proposed by phase bob-cli-an.6.4 (PROPOSED FOLLOW-UP): the loopback bind narrowed who can reach /sendmail, but its brute-force suspension can still be bypassed by any local client.

payload.description: aw bound 23401 to loopback; this hardens the token suspension behind it
